info.title: GoBTC Pay Merchant Account API
info.description:
# GoBTC Pay — Merchant Account API

Backwards compatibility is preserved across published versions. Found an error in the docs? Email [support@gomining.com](mailto:support@gomining.com).

This is the **Merchant dashboard** surface of the GoBTC Pay API.

Endpoints for the merchant personal cabinet (stores, POS terminals, team,
reports, and webhooks). See the operation reference below.

## Webhooks

Configure outbound webhook endpoints so your backend is notified when a
payment's status changes — an alternative to polling the POS **Get payment**
endpoint.

- **Scope** — an endpoint can cover the whole account (`merchant`) or be
  narrowed to a single `store` or `pos` terminal.
- **Delivery** — the `payment.status.updated` event is `POST`ed as a thin
  envelope `{ eventId, type, createdAt, data }`, where `data` matches the POS
  **Get payment** response. Delivery is at-least-once — de-duplicate on
  `eventId`.
- **Signing** — each endpoint has its own `signingSecret` (returned once on
  create / rotate-secret). Verify the `X-GoBTCPay-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac>`
  header, where `v1 = HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, "{t}.{rawBody}")`, and
  reject deliveries outside a small time window.

Use **Send test event** to verify your receiver and signature validation.

merchantAuth.description: Merchant dashboard access token obtained from `/merchant/auth/login` (or the OAuth / passkey / 2FA login flows). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Refresh it via `/merchant/auth/refresh` when it expires.

post.description: Creates a payment request for a POS terminal. Specify the `amount` and `currency`; the response includes the satoshi amount, the BTC price snapshot, an `expiresAt` deadline, and a `qrString` to present to the payer. `signature` and `ts` may be supplied for request signing.

amount.description: Amount to charge, in the selected fiat `currency`.

description.description: Optional description shown to the payer.

metadata.description: Internal system metadata attached to the payment (reserved; not set by clients).

ttlSeconds.description: Optional lifetime of the payment in seconds; after this it expires.

externalId.description: Merchant's own correlation id (e.g. order / invoice id). Unique per merchant, so reusing it makes create-payment idempotent. Echoed back in payment responses and webhook deliveries.

signature.description: Optional HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request (hex), authenticating the POS terminal with its `apiKey`.

ts.description: Request timestamp in milliseconds, used together with `signature` for replay protection.

txid.description: On-chain Bitcoin transaction id (hex) of this receipt. Look it up in any block explorer to show the payer their transaction.

amountSats.description: What this transaction paid into **this payment's** address, in satoshis — not the transaction's total, which may pay other outputs as well.

blockHeight.description: Height of the block that included the transaction; `null` while it is still in the mempool.

blockTime.description: Timestamp of that block, Unix seconds; `null` while the transaction is still in the mempool. Historical payments confirmed before this field existed report `null` permanently.

confirmations.description: Confirmations as of **now**, not as of the moment the payment was paid, so the value keeps growing. `0` — seen but not in a block yet. `null` — the current chain tip is not known to us right now, so the count cannot be stated; do not render it as zero, the transaction may well be deeply confirmed. The remaining fields are unaffected.

feeSats.description: Network fee the payer paid for this transaction, in satoshis; `null` when it is not known to us.

transactions.description: On-chain transactions observed paying this payment, freshest first. Empty until something is seen — and empty is a normal state for a payment in `initiated`. More than one element means the payer sent more than one transaction (an overpayment or a top-up); sum `amountSats` across the list to get what actually arrived. Identical for both payment routes: an in-app payment reports its single transaction here just like one paid from an external wallet.

paidAt.description: When the payment was paid, Unix timestamp (seconds); `null` until then. This is the payment's settlement time — for when a single transaction was mined see `transactions[].blockTime`.

post.description: Custodial counterpart of **Register**: creates the cabinet user and a custodial merchant, then creates that merchant's Uphold business user and its BTC account. Alongside `email` / `password` it takes the legal entity details Uphold requires — `businessEmail`, `country`, `subdivision`, `legalEntityType` — and the accepted `termsOfService` code, which is recorded together with the time and the caller's IP. Returns the new `userId` and `status`. The Uphold half is best-effort: if it fails the registration still stands, and the entities are replayed by **Create Uphold entities**.

displayName.description: Public display name shown to payers (optional).

post.description: Replays the creation of the signed-in custodial merchant's Uphold business user and BTC account for the case where that step did not go through during **Register (custodial)**. Takes no parameters — everything it needs, including the recorded Terms of Service acceptance, was stored at registration. Idempotent: once the entities exist the call is a no-op and never creates a second pair.

Custodial merchants only — a non-custodial merchant gets an error rather than zeroes. Returns the merchant's money as three non-overlapping levels in satoshi, so every satoshi is counted exactly once: `inTransitSats` (paid by the buyer, not yet credited to the platform Treasury, gross), `pendingPayoutSats` (credited but not yet paid out — net of the platform fee, and including amounts held by a blocked payout), and `availableSats` (on the merchant's own Uphold account and free to dispose of: the balance Uphold reports as available, minus `reservedSats`). `reservedSats` covers withdrawals the merchant has started that Uphold has not debited yet, and is `0` until withdrawals exist. `balanceAsOf` is the unix second the figures are current as of. `balanceStale` is true when the Uphold balance could not be refreshed: `availableSats` is then the last value seen and must not be shown as current — it is never replaced by a figure computed from our own data. `upholdAccountReady` is false while the merchant's Uphold account has not been created yet, which is why `availableSats` is `0`. `payoutBlocked` is present only while something holds the payout back, carrying a machine-readable `reason` and a `message` for the merchant.

Custodial merchants only — a non-custodial merchant gets an error rather than an empty list. Returns what Uphold currently allows the merchant's account to do, taken from the stored snapshot: the call never queries Uphold itself. Each entry of `capabilities` carries Uphold's `code` and `name`, whether it is `enabled`, the `requirements` still **missing** (a non-empty list means the capability does not pass even when `enabled` is true), the `restrictions` in force, and `required` — whether the platform needs it for the merchant to operate. `checkedAt` is the unix second of the last successful check, `null` when none ever succeeded; `capabilities` is then empty because the state is unknown, not because nothing is required. `stale` is true when the last refresh attempt failed, with the reason in `lastError` — the state shown is the last good one and may be out of date, which on its own does not block anything. `actionsBlocked` says whether the merchant's actions (creating payments, sending the payout) are being refused, and `blockingCodes` lists the required capabilities that do not pass. Requirement and restriction codes are free-form strings: Uphold introduces new ones without notice, so show a code you do not recognize as it is.

Custodial merchants only. Saves a BTC wallet the merchant can later withdraw to. Takes the `address`, an optional `label`, and a `totpCode` — adding a destination is a sensitive action and is gated by the merchant's TOTP. Returns the saved wallet: its `id`, `merchantId`, `address`, `label`, `network`, and `createdAt`. There is no asset field — a custodial merchant only ever holds bitcoin.

post.description: Custodial merchants only. Starts a withdrawal of `amountSats` (before fees, in satoshi) from the merchant's Uphold balance to a saved wallet (`walletId`), gated by `totpCode`. Returns the created withdrawal with the quote it was accepted under in `feeSummary` (`amountSats`, `feeSats`, `receivedSats` and Uphold's `feeBreakdown` line items, all in satoshi). `status` is `pending`, or `awaiting_travel_rule` when Uphold requires Travel Rule information first. Typed failures include `insufficient_available_balance`, `amount_below_minimum`, `pending_withdrawal_exists`, `fee_exceeds_amount`, `wallet_not_found`, the address checks (`address_validation_failed`, `address_wrong_network`, `address_not_btc`), the TOTP checks (`totp_required`, `totp_invalid`, `totp_not_configured`), and the eligibility checks (`not_custodial_merchant`, `no_uphold_account`, `withdraw_not_configured`).

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

createdAt.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

post.description: Custodial merchants only. Returns the merchant's withdrawals, newest first, as `items` with a `totalCount`. Every filter is optional: `status` narrows to one lifecycle state, `from` / `to` bound the creation time (inclusive unix seconds), and `limit` / `skip` page the result.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

createdAt.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

totalCount.description: Total number of records matching the filters.

post.description: Custodial merchants only. Fetches one withdrawal by `withdrawalId`. The withdrawal must belong to the authenticated merchant. Returns the full withdrawal item, including its quote (`quotedFeeSats`, `quotedReceivedSats`), the actual fee once settled (`feeSats`, `receivedSats`, `feeBreakdown` — `null` until then), `onchainTxid`, and the lifecycle timestamps.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

createdAt.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

post.description: Custodial merchants only. Cancels a withdrawal that has not been handed to Uphold yet, releasing the reserved funds and moving it to `canceled`. Returns `{ ok: true }` — the outcome is single-valued, so a failure arrives as a typed error rather than as a withdrawal in another state. An already submitted withdrawal returns `withdrawal_already_submitted`, and one past submission returns `withdrawal_not_cancellable`.

Custodial merchants only. Opens an Uphold Travel Rule verification session for a withdrawal Uphold is holding (`awaiting_travel_rule`). Returns what Uphold's embedded widget needs to mount, relayed verbatim: `flow`, the widget `url`, a short-lived `token`, and provider-specific `data`. Safe to call repeatedly — nothing about the session is stored, and an expired one is replaced by asking again.

url.description: Destination URL that receives webhook deliveries.

post.description: Custodial merchants only. Submits the Travel Rule information the merchant completed in Uphold's widget for a held withdrawal. `payload` is the widget's `complete` result **whole**, including its nested `value` — Uphold requires the envelope intact, so it is required and forwarded verbatim; its inner shape is Uphold's. On success the withdrawal leaves `awaiting_travel_rule` and returns to `pending` for re-evaluation, which is the item returned.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

createdAt.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

Human-readable label for the POS terminal (optional).

post.description: Soft-deletes the bank account. Fails with `bank_account_has_pending_offramp` if there is an in-flight off-ramp using it. Gated by 2FA (`totpCode`). Returns `{ ok }`.

Prices an off-ramp without starting one: what `amountSats` BTC becomes in USD on the bank account identified by `bankAccountId`, what the conversion costs, and how long that price holds. `amountSats` must be a whole number of satoshi greater than zero. Returns an `approvedQuote` — the signed terms `offramp/create` executes on (`terms` with `merchantId`, `quoteId`, `amountSats`, `feeSats`, `netSats`, `bankAccountId`, `destinationAmount`, `destinationAsset`, `exchangeRate`, `expiresAt` and `travelRuleWillBeRequired`, plus a `signature` over them) — and a `feeBreakdown` for display. Satoshi values inside `terms` are decimal strings, which is what they are on the wire in both directions. Render every figure from `terms`: it is the only copy, so there is no second one to disagree with it. Store the `approvedQuote` exactly as received and send it back unmodified; read the countdown from `approvedQuote.terms.expiresAt`. Fails with `quote_failed` when the provider would not price it — never with a zero fee or a zero rate standing in for a price. Creates no off-ramp, reserves no balance and needs no 2FA — nothing moves until the merchant approves the quote by passing the whole `approvedQuote` to `offramp/create`.

merchantId.description: The merchant these terms were issued to. Terms presented by anyone else are refused even though their signature is genuine.

quoteId.description: Uphold's identifier for this exact price.

amountSats.description: Gross BTC debited from the merchant's Uphold account, in satoshis, as a decimal string. A string because that is what satoshi values are on the wire in both directions, and because a signed value must have exactly one representation — send it back character for character.

feeSats.description: Cost of the conversion as quoted, in satoshis, as a decimal string — Uphold's fee for this transfer, not a Bitcoin network fee. Zero is a legitimate quote.

netSats.description: What is left of `amountSats` after `feeSats`, in satoshis, as a decimal string — the BTC actually converted.

bankAccountId.description: The registered bank account the USD is paid out to.

destinationAmount.description: What arrives at the bank, in `destinationAsset`, as quoted.

destinationAsset.description: Currency the payout arrives in, e.g. `USD`.

exchangeRate.description: Rate this quote converts at. Signed rather than merely displayed: `offramp/create` rebuilds its answer from these terms and cannot ask the provider again.

expiresAt.description: When this price stops holding, Unix timestamp (seconds). Confirming after it fails with `quote_expired`; request a fresh quote and have the merchant approve that one. Show the countdown from here — this is the value `offramp/create` enforces.

travelRuleWillBeRequired.description: Whether Uphold will demand Travel Rule information for this transfer. Signed because it decides the state the off-ramp starts in — `awaiting_travel_rule` rather than `pending` — so it is not a warning a client may adjust. Distinct from the record's `travelRuleRequired`, which means the off-ramp is waiting for that data right now.

terms.description: The terms being approved. This is exactly what the `signature` covers.

signature.description: The platform's signature over `terms`. Opaque to clients: pass it back unchanged, do not parse it and do not attempt to produce one.

approvedQuote.description: The quote the merchant approved, signed by the platform. Store it exactly as received and send it back to `offramp/create` whole — the amount, the bank account and the fee are read from it rather than from request fields, and any edit invalidates the `signature`.

post.description: Executes an off-ramp the merchant has already approved: send back the `approvedQuote` returned by `offramp/quote` **whole and unmodified** — byte for byte, including the decimal-string satoshi values — together with a 2FA code (`totpCode`). The amount, the bank account, the fee and the whole quoted price are **not** sent as fields — they are taken from `approvedQuote.terms`, whose `signature` the platform verifies before using them, so what executes is the price that was shown, and the `feeSummary` in the answer is rebuilt from those same terms. Fails with `quote_not_found` when the terms do not verify for this merchant — a forged signature, an edited term and terms issued to someone else all answer the same way — and `quote_expired` when `terms.expiresAt` has passed, in which case the merchant approves a fresh quote; the platform never re-prices silently. Returns the created off-ramp with the `feeSummary` that was executed. When `travelRuleRequired` is true the off-ramp starts in `awaiting_travel_rule`.

merchantId.description: The merchant these terms were issued to. Terms presented by anyone else are refused even though their signature is genuine.

quoteId.description: Uphold's identifier for this exact price.

amountSats.description: Gross BTC debited from the merchant's Uphold account, in satoshis, as a decimal string. A string because that is what satoshi values are on the wire in both directions, and because a signed value must have exactly one representation — send it back character for character.

feeSats.description: Cost of the conversion as quoted, in satoshis, as a decimal string — Uphold's fee for this transfer, not a Bitcoin network fee. Zero is a legitimate quote.

netSats.description: What is left of `amountSats` after `feeSats`, in satoshis, as a decimal string — the BTC actually converted.

bankAccountId.description: The registered bank account the USD is paid out to.

destinationAmount.description: What arrives at the bank, in `destinationAsset`, as quoted.

destinationAsset.description: Currency the payout arrives in, e.g. `USD`.

exchangeRate.description: Rate this quote converts at. Signed rather than merely displayed: `offramp/create` rebuilds its answer from these terms and cannot ask the provider again.

expiresAt.description: When this price stops holding, Unix timestamp (seconds). Confirming after it fails with `quote_expired`; request a fresh quote and have the merchant approve that one. Show the countdown from here — this is the value `offramp/create` enforces.

travelRuleWillBeRequired.description: Whether Uphold will demand Travel Rule information for this transfer. Signed because it decides the state the off-ramp starts in — `awaiting_travel_rule` rather than `pending` — so it is not a warning a client may adjust. Distinct from the record's `travelRuleRequired`, which means the off-ramp is waiting for that data right now.

signature.description: The platform's signature over `terms`. Opaque to clients: pass it back unchanged, do not parse it and do not attempt to produce one.

post.description: Cancels the off-ramp identified by `offrampId` while it has not yet been submitted to Uphold. Fails with `offramp_already_submitted` once it has left the platform. Returns `{ ok }`.

Opens an Uphold Travel Rule widget session for the off-ramp identified by `offrampId`, bound to its quote. Returns the session Uphold issued, relayed verbatim: `flow`, the `url` the widget mounts, a short-lived `token` and provider-specific `data` forwarded unchanged. Mount the widget with it and let the merchant complete the form there — the personal details go to the provider, never to this API. There is no expiry to compare against: the session is short-lived and single-use, so call this again to replace a stale one.

flow.description: Which Uphold widget form to mount.

url.description: Base URL the Uphold Travel Rule widget mounts from.

token.description: Short-lived auth token for this widget session.

data.description: Provider-specific initialization data for the widget, forwarded unchanged. Its shape is Uphold's and changes without notice — hand it to the widget rather than reading it.

post.description: Asks whether the Travel Rule requirement on `offrampId` has been closed, after the merchant has finished in the widget. Takes nothing else: the platform collects no personal data and forwards none, so there is no payload to send and no session to identify — it reads the quote from the off-ramp and asks Uphold for the status of the request for information on it. Returns `released` — whether the off-ramp left `awaiting_travel_rule` and is executing again — and the `status` behind it: `cleared` (closed, released), `pending` (evidence still settling — wait and call again, the same session stands), `failed` (rejected — open a **new** session and redo), `expired` (lapsed — also a new session), `unchecked` (no request for information, or Uphold could not be asked — released anyway, since not knowing is not a refusal). Branch on `released`; show `status`. Safe to call repeatedly.

status.description: Uphold's verdict on the request for information attached to the quote — **not** a payment or off-ramp status. `cleared`: closed, the off-ramp is released. `pending`: the evidence is still settling, wait and call again with the same session. `failed`: rejected — the merchant needs a **new** session. `expired`: the requirement lapsed — also a new session. `unchecked`: there is no such request, or Uphold could not be asked, and the off-ramp is released anyway because not knowing is not a refusal.

released.description: Whether the off-ramp left `awaiting_travel_rule` and is executing again. Branch on this. It follows `status` exactly — true for `cleared` and `unchecked`, false for `pending`, `failed` and `expired` — and the two can never disagree: a response pairing them any other way is rejected.

post.description: Creates a payment from the merchant cabinet. Authorization is the merchant bearer token — no `posTerminalId` or signature is sent: the payment is booked on the merchant's system POS (created lazily on first use). Specify the `amount` and `currency`; the response includes the satoshi amount, the BTC price snapshot, an `expiresAt` deadline, and a `qrString` to present to the payer. Pass an optional `externalId` (your order / invoice id) to make the call idempotent.

txid.description: On-chain Bitcoin transaction id (hex) of this receipt. Look it up in any block explorer to show the payer their transaction.

amountSats.description: What this transaction paid into **this payment's** address, in satoshis — not the transaction's total, which may pay other outputs as well.

blockHeight.description: Height of the block that included the transaction; `null` while it is still in the mempool.

blockTime.description: Timestamp of that block, Unix seconds; `null` while the transaction is still in the mempool. Historical payments confirmed before this field existed report `null` permanently.

confirmations.description: Confirmations as of **now**, not as of the moment the payment was paid, so the value keeps growing. `0` — seen but not in a block yet. `null` — the current chain tip is not known to us right now, so the count cannot be stated; do not render it as zero, the transaction may well be deeply confirmed. The remaining fields are unaffected.

feeSats.description: Network fee the payer paid for this transaction, in satoshis; `null` when it is not known to us.

transactions.description: On-chain transactions observed paying this payment, freshest first. Empty until something is seen — and empty is a normal state for a payment in `initiated`. More than one element means the payer sent more than one transaction (an overpayment or a top-up); sum `amountSats` across the list to get what actually arrived. Identical for both payment routes: an in-app payment reports its single transaction here just like one paid from an external wallet.

paidAt.description: When the payment was paid, Unix timestamp (seconds); `null` until then. This is the payment's settlement time — for when a single transaction was mined see `transactions[].blockTime`.

posTerminalLocation.description: Location of the POS terminal (may be null).

settledAt.description: When the payment was credited to the platform, Unix timestamp (seconds).

status.description: Result of the credit: `settled` — credited to the platform; `reversed` — the credit was rolled back.

platformFeeSats.description: Platform fee withheld from this payment, in satoshis. `null` when the fee is not known for this payment (credited before fees were introduced) — not zero.

netSats.description: Credited to the merchant **for this payment**, in satoshis: the payment amount minus the withheld platform fee. `null` when the fee is unknown, together with `platformFeeSats`. This is the payment's own share — for the total transferred see `settlement.payout.batchAmountSats`.

status.description: State of the payout: `preparing` — assembled and on its way out; `processing` — submitted, not finished yet; `on_hold` — held by Uphold (typically a compliance check); `completed` — the money reached the merchant's account; `failed` — the transfer did not go through; `blocked` — the platform is holding it back, see `blockedReason`.

submittedAt.description: When the payout was submitted for transfer, Unix timestamp (seconds); `null` while it is still being prepared or is blocked.

completedAt.description: When the payout finished, Unix timestamp (seconds); `null` until then.

upholdTransactionId.description: Id of the transfer in Uphold, once there is one; `null` otherwise.

blockedReason.description: Why the payout is being held back — set when `status` is `blocked`, `null` otherwise.

batchAmountSats.description: Total amount of the **whole payout**, in satoshis. One payout covers several payments, so this is normally larger than what this payment contributed — that figure is `settlement.netSats`. **Absent** for a credential limited to one store or to a set of POS terminals: a payout is assembled per merchant, so this total covers stores such a credential has no access to. Absent means not disclosed to you, not zero.

batchPaymentCount.description: How many payments this payout covers, including the current one. **Absent** for a credential limited to one store or to a set of POS terminals, for the same reason as `batchAmountSats` — and absent means not disclosed to you, not a payout of no payments.

payout.description: The payout this payment was paid out by. `null` — the payment is credited to the platform but no payout has been assembled yet.

settlement.description: How this payment was settled with the platform: when it was credited, what fee was withheld, and the payout it was paid out by. `null` — the payment did not go through the custodial path (funds went straight to the merchant's own wallet) or has not been credited yet. Absent settlement means no credit happened, not a credit of zero.

post.description:
The non-custodial merchant's own money, split into three non-overlapping levels: `connectedWalletSats` (confirmed on the reserved `0/0` address), `paymentWalletsSats` (confirmed on the per-payment addresses of payments that are `detected`, `paid` or `cleared`) and `inFlightSats` (still unconfirmed in the mempool, and **signed** — negative means an outgoing spend not yet in a block).

All figures come from the chain, never from the payment ledger: the platform does not see the merchant's outgoing transactions, so a ledger-derived number would be total receipts rather than a balance. When the chain cannot be reached the last known values are returned with `balanceStale: true` — they are never substituted with an internally computed amount. `addressesTruncated: true` means the merchant holds funds on more addresses than one refresh may query, so the totals are incomplete and must be presented as such.

Custodial merchants are rejected: their funds sit on the platform treasury address, see **Custodial balance**.

Paginated list of the non-custodial merchant's addresses that currently hold money — the connected `0/0` address and the per-payment addresses under observation. Each row carries `address`, `kind` (`connected` / `payment`), `derivationPath`, `paymentId` (`null` for the connected wallet), `confirmedSats` and `inFlightSats`. Addresses with a zero total are omitted. Custodial merchants are rejected — they have no addresses of their own.
